newsitem.title: USA: Lilly posts record third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Lilly posts record third quarter.

text.p: Lilly Industries Inc. Monday reported record third-quarter results, boosted by the acquisition of Guardsman Products, Inc. and improved sales across the company's entire product line.

Lilly, one of the largest North American manufacturers of industrial coatings and speciality chemical products, said profits jumped 53 percent to $7.0 million, or 30 cents a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 31, from $4.6 million, or 20 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales surged 89 percent to a record $150.9 million from $79.7 million.

Lilly said it expects operating profits for fiscal 1996 will exceed those of a year ago, excluding a one-time restructuring expense of $9.6 million incurred in the second quarter for the acquisition of Guardsman Products in April.
Lilly Chairman Douglas Huemme said the integration of the Guardsman business has already cut about $15 million in "redundant costs" on an annual basis, and was a major factor in raising profits.

He said Lilly's original expectations that the merger will cut operating expenses by at least $20 million over the next 12 to 24 months was proving to be conservative. Savings of at least $25 million are now "more probable," he said.
Huemme said he expects continuing profit growth during the final three months of the fiscal year.

Lilly also said it purchased a powder coatings manufacturing plant in University Research Park in Charlotte, N.C. The company said the new plant gives it the capacity to roughly double its powder coatings sales.
"Powder coatings is our fastest growing product line, and the opportunity to expand this business is strategic to our growth plans," Huemme said.
Lilly's stock rose 12.5 cents to $17.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
